chunk_findings.detail: The generated CLI form is not a reliable exact next call because `joined` is interpolated without quoting. For the common case of one undeclared directory, `update_call("t1", [], ["src/*"])` returns `` `ddflow update t1 --globs src/*` ``. When pasted into a shell, `src/*` is expanded to the files currently in `src`, so the CLI receives multiple arguments instead of the single glob `src/*`; with a path containing spaces, e.g. `my dir/*`, it is split into two arguments. If the joined value is empty, the CLI form becomes `--globs ` with no argument. This violates the requirement that notices name the exact copyable CLI call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:63-69 `update_call`

chunk_findings.detail: A diff containing only ddflow's own bookkeeping files is treated as evidence that the task's declared globs were untouched. Given `changed_paths` returning `[".ddflow/ledger.json"]`, `it.globs == ["src/**"]`, and `cfg.locks.suggest_globs` true, `split` removes the own path, leaving `mine == []`, so `untouched == ["src/**"]` and `keep == []`. The function then emits a narrowing notice with `update_call(item_id, [], [])`, i.e. an empty `--globs` call, even though no task-owned file has been written and narrowing is not yet knowable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:102-121 `untouched_report`

chunk_findings.detail: When the changed-path reader returns `None`, `add_notice` appends the `UNKNOWN` string as a warning. That warning says only that the check did not run; it does not name the exact next CLI/MCP call, contrary to the stated conformance rule that every refusal or notice names the next call [D-tell-dont-discover]. For example, with `changed_paths` returning `None` and `undeclared_write = "warn"`, the user gets “could not tell what this task changed …” but no `ddflow ...` or `ddflow_task ...` follow-up.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:19 `UNKNOWN` / `add_notice`

chunk_findings.detail: With `[locks].undeclared_write = "block"`, a task that writes a file outside its declared globs only gets a `NOTE:` appended to the status text. `_glob_notes` uses `OG.undeclared_report` solely as a display string, and `_query` still returns `O.ok("gate.status", status=plain(s), ...)` unconditionally. The "block" knob therefore never blocks the gate for undeclared writes: the returned outcome remains ok and the status is the original pre-note `s`, not a blocked/refused status. This makes the advertised block setting a no-op at the gate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates/_query.py:_glob_notes

chunk_findings.detail: When all declared globs are untouched but the diff has changes outside them, `keep` becomes empty. Then `update_call(item_id, keep, [])` produces `` `ddflow update item --globs ` `` with no value. That is not a usable CLI call: the shell/argparse sees `--globs` with no argument, and the advertised “exact next call” is malformed. Example input: item globs are `["docs/**"]` and changed files are `["src/main.py"]`; `keep` is empty and the returned command errors instead of narrowing the claim.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:untouched_report

chunk_findings.detail: `update_call` joins globs with commas but never quotes or escapes them, so a valid path segment containing a space makes the CLI form wrong. For an undeclared file `docs/my notes/a.py`, `directory_globs` returns `docs/my notes/*`, and the CLI form becomes ``ddflow update item --globs docs/my notes/*``. In a shell this parses as `--globs docs/my` and a separate `notes/*` argument, so the command does not declare the intended files; the advertised “exact call” is therefore not exact.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:update_call

chunk_findings.detail: The monkeypatch in `test_block_blocks_only_a_known_write_never_unknown` uses the wrong reader contract. The reader returned by `_reader` has signature `(repo, item) -> list[str] | None`, and the public APIs consume it directly, so `mod._read` must itself be such a reader. With `mod._read = lambda read: _reader({"T": ["z/1"]})`, invoking `verdict_notice(st, cfg, "T", REPO)` makes `_read(REPO, item)` return the inner lambda `lambda repo, it: table[it.id]` instead of `["z/1"]`. The resulting function is not a file list; when `verdict_notice`/`undeclared_report` iterates it to compute undeclared writes, Python raises `TypeError: 'function' object is not iterable`, so the test never reaches the intended assertion. The same bad patch is applied again at line 77 for the `warn` case.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_observed_globs.py:69

chunk_findings.detail: `_glob_notes` treats `s.current == ""` as if the task were merge-ready and calls `OG.untouched_report`. If an item has no current phase/gate yet (the code’s own condition includes empty string), `gate.status` will compare the declared lease globs with the files written so far—none—and report every declared glob as untouched, offering to narrow it before any work has started. For example, a newly added task declared with `docs/**` and `src/**` but with `s.current == ""` will get a “narrow these globs” note even though it is not merge-ready, which can cause the operator to shrink globs away from files the task will later write.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/gates/_query.py:_glob_notes

chunk_findings.detail: `_habits` assumes every finished task has an iterable `globs` attribute: when `changed_paths` returns a non-`None` list, it evaluates `split(changed, list(o.globs))`. Other functions in this same module treat `globs` as optional/possibly `None` (`it.globs or []` in `learned_report`, `if not it.globs` in `undeclared_report`/`untouched_report`). If a finished same-tag task has `globs = None` (i.e. no declared globs) and its changed file list is known, `learned()` raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable` instead of treating that task’s declaration as empty and counting its undeclared writes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:140

chunk_findings.detail: `UNKNOWN` is returned verbatim by `undeclared_report` and then appended by `add_notice`, but it contains `<id>` placeholders instead of the actual item id. For item `abc`, the warning says to re-run `ddflow gate status <id>` and `ddflow_gate action=status id=<id>`, not the exact next call for `abc`. This violates the stated conformance requirement that every refusal/notice name the exact next CLI and MCP call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:18

chunk_findings.detail: `update_call` quotes the CLI `--globs` argument with `shlex.quote(joined)`, but emits the MCP form as `globs={joined}` with no quoting. If a task writes a path containing a space, e.g. `my dir/a.py`, `directory_globs` produces `my dir/*` and the returned MCP fragment becomes `globs=my dir/*`, which is not a single value and can be parsed as multiple arguments or rejected. The CLI form is safe, but the “exact MCP call” is wrong for such paths.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:71

chunk_findings.detail: In `_habits` the past-task loop calls `split(changed, list(o.globs))` without treating `o.globs` as optional. `undeclared_report` and `learned_report` explicitly guard `it.globs` as possibly absent, so a done same-tag task with `globs=None` is a valid state record. That input makes `list(None)` raise `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable`, crashing `learned`/`learned_report`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:_habits

chunk_findings.detail: The branch `if not it.globs: return ""` disables the undeclared-write gate for a task with no declared globs. Given an open task with `it.globs == []` and `changed == ["src/foo.py"]`, every written file is outside the (empty) declaration, which is exactly the undeclared write this gate must surface. Because the function returns an empty string, `verdict_notice` emits no warning and no block even with `undeclared_write = "block"`, contradicting the intent that undeclared writes are surfaced at the gate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:undeclared_report

chunk_findings.detail: The test monkeypatches the module-level reader as `mod._read = lambda read: _reader({"T": ["z/1"]})` (and the `{"T": None}` variant). Every other call site in this file establishes the reader contract as a two-argument callable `(repo, item) -> list[str] | None` via `_reader` and the `read=` arguments to `undeclared_report`, `untouched_report`, and `learned`. `verdict_notice` is called without a `read=` argument, so it must invoke this module-level reader as `_read(repo, item)`. The one-argument lambda raises `TypeError` on that call instead of returning the intended `["z/1"]` or `None`, so the test does not exercise block/warn behavior and will fail when run.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_observed_globs.py:test_block_blocks_only_a_known_write_never_unknown

That means when every declared glob is untouched—e.g. a merge-ready task declared `docs/**` but actually wrote `src/m.py`—the gate offers no narrowing/removal of the stale declared glob. This contradicts the stated behavior that declared-but-untouched globs are offered for narrowing at merge-ready, and it specifically suppresses the feature for the measured `docs/**` case where the task touched none of its declared files.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `if not keep: return ""` suppresses the declared-but-untouched notice exactly when every declared glob is untouched. Given a merge-ready task with `it.globs = ["docs/**", "src/**"]` and `_read(...)` returning `["tests/foo.py"]`, `split` will return `untouched == ["docs/**", "src/**"]`, so `keep == []` and the function returns `""`. These globs are still declared-but-untouched and, per the change's stated intent, must be offered for narrowing at merge-ready; the undeclared-write notice's update call is built from `old globs + tests/*`, so it keeps them rather than narrowing. This leaves stale declarations locked with no offered corrective call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:untouched_report

chunk_findings.detail: The new test asserts `OG.untouched_report(st, Config(), "T", repo=REPO, read=_reader({"T": ["src/m.py"]})) == ""` for a task declared with `["docs/**"]`. At merge-ready, `docs/**` is a declared-but-untouched glob, which the change intent says must be offered for narrowing. This input makes the suite bless the wrong behavior: the required narrowing offer is absent, and a correct non-empty report for this scenario would fail the test. The undeclared-write path for `src/m.py` does not cover the distinct declared-but-untouched `docs/**` glob.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_observed_globs.py:test_no_narrowing_is_offered_when_every_glob_is_untouched

chunk_findings.detail: The replacement checks only `"gate status T" in OG.unknown("T")`. It never asserts the MCP form, e.g. `ddflow_gate action=status id=T`. Since the original defect required exact CLI and MCP forms, an `OG.unknown` implementation that substitutes `<id>` in the CLI half but still leaves `<id>` in the MCP half would pass every assertion in this delta, leaving the conformance requirement unverified.

This violates the stated conformance requirement that every refusal/notice name the exact next CLI and MCP call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:18

chunk_findings.detail: `update_call` quotes the CLI `--globs` argument with `shlex.quote(joined)`, but emits the MCP form as `globs={joined}` with no quoting. If a task writes a path containing a space, e.g. `my dir/a.py`, `directory_globs` produces `my dir/*` and the returned MCP fragment becomes `globs=my dir/*`, which is not a single value and can be parsed as multiple arguments or rejected. The CLI form is safe, but the “exact MCP call” is wrong for such paths.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:71

chunk_findings.detail: In `_habits` the past-task loop calls `split(changed, list(o.globs))` without treating `o.globs` as optional. `undeclared_report` and `learned_report` explicitly guard `it.globs` as possibly absent, so a done same-tag task with `globs=None` is a valid state record. That input makes `list(None)` raise `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable`, crashing `learned`/`learned_report`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:_habits

chunk_findings.detail: The branch `if not it.globs: return ""` disables the undeclared-write gate for a task with no declared globs. Given an open task with `it.globs == []` and `changed == ["src/foo.py"]`, every written file is outside the (empty) declaration, which is exactly the undeclared write this gate must surface. Because the function returns an empty string, `verdict_notice` emits no warning and no block even with `undeclared_write = "block"`, contradicting the intent that undeclared writes are surfaced at the gate.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:undeclared_report

chunk_findings.detail: The test monkeypatches the module-level reader as `mod._read = lambda read: _reader({"T": ["z/1"]})` (and the `{"T": None}` variant). Every other call site in this file establishes the reader contract as a two-argument callable `(repo, item) -> list[str] | None` via `_reader` and the `read=` arguments to `undeclared_report`, `untouched_report`, and `learned`. `verdict_notice` is called without a `read=` argument, so it must invoke this module-level reader as `_read(repo, item)`. The one-argument lambda raises `TypeError` on that call instead of returning the intended `["z/1"]` or `None`, so the test does not exercise block/warn behavior and will fail when run.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_observed_globs.py:test_block_blocks_only_a_known_write_never_unknown

chunk_findings.detail: The new test asserts that `OG.untouched_report(..., read=_reader({"T": ["src/m.py"]}))` returns `""` for a task whose only declared glob is `docs/**`. That means when every declared glob is untouched—e.g. a merge-ready task declared `docs/**` but actually wrote `src/m.py`—the gate offers no narrowing/removal of the stale declared glob. This contradicts the stated behavior that declared-but-untouched globs are offered for narrowing at merge-ready, and it specifically suppresses the feature for the measured `docs/**` case where the task touched none of its declared files.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_observed_globs.py:test_no_narrowing_is_offered_when_every_glob_is_untouched

chunk_findings.detail: The new `if not keep: return ""` suppresses the declared-but-untouched notice exactly when every declared glob is untouched. Given a merge-ready task with `it.globs = ["docs/**", "src/**"]` and `_read(...)` returning `["tests/foo.py"]`, `split` will return `untouched == ["docs/**", "src/**"]`, so `keep == []` and the function returns `""`. These globs are still declared-but-untouched and, per the change's stated intent, must be offered for narrowing at merge-ready; the undeclared-write notice's update call is built from `old globs + tests/*`, so it keeps them rather than narrowing. This leaves stale declarations locked with no offered corrective call.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:untouched_report

chunk_findings.detail: The new test asserts `OG.untouched_report(st, Config(), "T", repo=REPO, read=_reader({"T": ["src/m.py"]})) == ""` for a task declared with `["docs/**"]`. At merge-ready, `docs/**` is a declared-but-untouched glob, which the change intent says must be offered for narrowing. This input makes the suite bless the wrong behavior: the required narrowing offer is absent, and a correct non-empty report for this scenario would fail the test. The undeclared-write path for `src/m.py` does not cover the distinct declared-but-untouched `docs/**` glob.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_observed_globs.py:test_no_narrowing_is_offered_when_every_glob_is_untouched

chunk_findings.detail: The replacement checks only `"gate status T" in OG.unknown("T")`. It never asserts the MCP form, e.g. `ddflow_gate action=status id=T`. Since the original defect required exact CLI and MCP forms, an `OG.unknown` implementation that substitutes `<id>` in the CLI half but still leaves `<id>` in the MCP half would pass every assertion in this delta, leaving the conformance requirement unverified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_observed_globs.py:test_undeclared_report_clean_off_and_unknown

chunk_findings.detail: The new “re-declare” branch can reach the known unquoted MCP form in `update_call`. If a task is declared with `docs/**`, is merge-ready, and the reader reports `["my dir/a.py"]`, then every declared glob is untouched, `keep` is empty, `directory_globs(...)` produces `["my dir/*"]`, and line `update_call(item_id, [], wrote)` is used. The emitted MCP fragment is still `globs=my dir/*` (no quoting), so the “exact next MCP call” is not a single value and can be parsed as an extra argument. The new test only checks the CLI substring `--globs 'src/*'`, so it does not catch this malformed MCP form. This is the previously confirmed deferred `update_call` MCP-quoting defect, now reachable through the new re-declare notice; it violates the “exact next CLI and MCP call” requirement [r-tell-dont-discover].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:untouched_report

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding #4 remains in this delta: `update_call`’s MCP form is emitted as `globs=<joined>` without quoting. The new all-globs-untouched branch passes `wrote = directory_globs(split(changed, [])[0])` to `update_call`. For a merge-ready item whose only declared glob is untouched and whose written path is `my dir/a.py`, `directory_globs` produces `my dir/*`; the new notice then contains `globs=my dir/*` as the MCP call, which is not a single value and can be parsed as multiple arguments or rejected. The CLI half is quoted and safe, but the required exact MCP call is wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/observed_globs.py:128

chunk_findings.detail: The new test asserts only the CLI half of `OG.update_call`: `assert """--globs '["a,b/*"]'""" in OG.update_call("T", [], ["a,b/*"])`. It never checks the MCP half of the same call. The conformance requirement is that every refusal/notice names the exact next call in both CLI and MCP form, so this new JSON-list branch remains unverified for MCP: an implementation that fixed only the CLI form while still emitting a comma-split or placeholder MCP value would pass this test. The input `OG.update_call("T", [], ["a,b/*"])` produces an MCP fragment (`globs='["a,b/*"]'`), but no assertion confirms it is present or exact, unlike the neighboring `test_mcp_form_quotes_a_path_with_a_space`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_observed_globs.py:test_a_comma_in_a_glob_uses_the_json_list_form
